ideas.title: Add Search to PR List
ideas.description: Add search and filter functionality to the GitHub Pull Requests list, allowing users to quickly find PRs by title, author, or branch name.
ideas.rationale: The GitHub Issues list has comprehensive search/filter functionality (IssueListHeader with searchQuery, onSearchChange, filterState). The PRList component lacks this feature entirely despite handling similar list data. The useIssueFiltering hook pattern already exists and can be adapted for PRs.
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Create usePRFiltering hook based on existing useIssueFiltering pattern. 2. Add PRListHeader component mirroring IssueListHeader structure with search input. 3. Wire up filtering to PRList component. The search should filter by PR title, author.login, and headRefName fields.

ideas.title: Consolidate Filtering Hooks into Generic useFiltering
ideas.description: Create a generic useFiltering hook that can be used across GitHub Issues, Linear Issues, PRs, and other list components, reducing code duplication.
ideas.rationale: Two nearly identical useIssueFiltering hooks exist - one in github-issues/hooks and one in linear-import/hooks. Both implement similar search/filter logic that could be abstracted into a shared generic hook.
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Create generic useFiltering<T> hook in renderer/hooks/ that accepts items, searchQuery, and a searchFn predicate. 2. Refactor both useIssueFiltering hooks to use the new generic hook with domain-specific search predicates. 3. Export from hooks/index.ts for shared access.

ideas.title: Add Keyboard Shortcuts to Ideation Panel
ideas.description: Add keyboard shortcuts for common ideation actions: dismiss (D), convert to task (C), archive (A), select all (Ctrl+A), and refresh (R).
ideas.rationale: Keyboard shortcuts pattern exists in TaskEditDialog.tsx (Ctrl+Enter for submit) and App.tsx. The Ideation panel has frequent user actions (dismiss, convert, archive) that would benefit from keyboard acceleration. The store already has all the action methods.
existing_patterns: Keyboard shortcut registration pattern in App.tsx
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Add useEffect with keydown listener in Ideation.tsx for global shortcuts (R to refresh). 2. Add onKeyDown to IdeaCard for item-level shortcuts when focused (D to dismiss, C to convert, A to archive). 3. Show shortcuts in tooltips using existing Tooltip component pattern.

ideas.title: Create Shared GenericEmptyState Component
ideas.description: Extract the EmptyState pattern from github-issues into a shared, reusable component that other features can use for consistent empty state UI.
ideas.rationale: EmptyState component in github-issues/components/EmptyStates.tsx is well-designed with props for icon, message, and searchQuery handling. IdeationEmptyState and RoadmapEmptyState implement similar patterns separately. A shared component would ensure consistency and reduce duplication.
existing_patterns: EmptyState component structure with icon, message props
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Create GenericEmptyState in components/ui/empty-state.tsx with props: icon, title, description, searchQuery, actionButton. 2. Migrate github-issues EmptyState to use this shared component. 3. Refactor IdeationEmptyState and RoadmapEmptyState to use GenericEmptyState, passing domain-specific content.

ideas.title: Add Export to Markdown for Changelog Entries
ideas.description: Add ability to export changelog entries to a CHANGELOG.md file in the project root, formatted according to Keep a Changelog standard.
ideas.rationale: The changelog system has comprehensive formatter (formatter.ts), parser (parser.ts), and generator infrastructure but no export-to-file capability. The formatter already produces markdown-compatible output. This builds on existing changelog patterns to complete the workflow.
ideas.implementation_approach: 1. Create exporter.ts with exportToMarkdown(entries, projectPath) function using existing formatter. 2. Add exportChangelog IPC handler in changelog-handlers.ts. 3. Add export button to ChangelogHeader.tsx using existing Button component. 4. Write to {projectPath}/CHANGELOG.md with proper header and formatted entries.

ideas.title: Add Keyboard Focus Rings to Task Cards
ideas.description: Task cards are interactive elements that can be clicked but lack visible focus indicators when navigating with keyboard. Add focus-visible ring styles matching the existing button focus pattern.
ideas.rationale: Keyboard users cannot currently see which task card is focused, making keyboard navigation difficult. This violates WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 2.4.7 (Focus Visible) which requires a visible focus indicator for keyboard-navigable elements.
ideas.current_state: TaskCard uses Card component with cursor-pointer but no focus-visible styles. When users Tab through the interface, the task cards appear selected but have no visual focus ring. The Card component in ui/card.tsx doesn't include focus styles.
ideas.proposed_change: Add 'focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-background' classes to the Card component in TaskCard.tsx. Ensure the Card element is focusable with tabIndex={0} and add role='button' aria-label={task.title} for semantic correctness.
ideas.user_benefit: Keyboard users can clearly see which task card is focused, enabling efficient keyboard navigation through the Kanban board without needing a mouse.

ideas.title: Add aria-labels to Icon-Only Buttons
ideas.description: Several icon-only buttons throughout the application lack proper aria-labels, making them inaccessible to screen reader users. The Add, Archive, and Help buttons are particularly affected.
ideas.rationale: Screen reader users cannot understand the purpose of icon-only buttons without aria-labels. Using only title attributes is insufficient as they are not reliably announced by screen readers. This violates WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
ideas.current_state: Icon-only buttons like Plus (add task), Archive, and Help use title={} for tooltips but lack aria-label attributes. Examples: KanbanBoard line 119-127 has Plus button without aria-label; line 129-137 has Archive button without aria-label. Sidebar Help button at line 348 also lacks aria-label.
ideas.proposed_change: Add aria-label to all icon-only buttons: 1) Add aria-label='Add new task to backlog' to Plus button in KanbanBoard DroppableColumn, 2) Add aria-label='Archive all completed tasks' to Archive button, 3) Add aria-label='Get help and support' to HelpCircle button in Sidebar. Pattern: <Button aria-label='Descriptive action label'>
ideas.user_benefit: Screen reader users can understand the purpose of each icon button and effectively navigate and interact with the application.

ideas.title: Add Live Region for Form Error Announcements
ideas.description: Form validation errors appear visually but are not announced to screen readers. Add aria-live regions to error messages in forms like TaskCreationWizard, AddProjectModal, and settings forms.
ideas.rationale: When form submission fails or validation errors occur, sighted users see the error but screen reader users are not notified. This creates a confusing experience where the form appears to do nothing. WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.3 (Status Messages) requires programmatic announcement of status changes.
ideas.current_state: TaskCreationWizard displays errors in a styled div (lines 1111-1116) but has no aria-live attribute. The error div contains visual styling with destructive colors but no semantic announcement mechanism for assistive technology.
ideas.proposed_change: Add role='alert' and aria-atomic='true' to error message containers. In TaskCreationWizard line 1111, update error div to: <div role='alert' aria-atomic='true' aria-live='assertive' className='flex items-start gap-2 rounded-lg bg-destructive/10 border border-destructive/30 p-3 text-sm text-destructive'>. Apply same pattern to all form error displays across the codebase.
ideas.user_benefit: Screen reader users are immediately notified when form errors occur, allowing them to understand what went wrong and take corrective action without visual cues.

ideas.title: Improve Touch Target Sizes for Mobile
ideas.description: Several interactive elements have touch targets smaller than the recommended 44x44px minimum, particularly image thumbnail remove buttons and column header icon buttons.
ideas.rationale: The image thumbnail remove buttons in TaskCreationWizard are 16x16px (h-4 w-4 class), significantly below the WCAG 2.5.5 recommended 44x44px touch target. This makes them difficult to tap accurately on touch devices and causes frustration for mobile users.
ideas.current_state: Image thumbnail remove buttons at TaskCreationWizard line 847 use 'h-4 w-4' (16x16px). Column header icon buttons in KanbanBoard use 'h-7 w-7' (28x28px). Both are below the 44x44px recommended minimum for reliable touch interaction.
ideas.proposed_change: 1) For image remove buttons: increase hit area using a larger wrapper while keeping icon visually small. Change 'h-4 w-4' button to 'h-8 w-8 p-2' wrapper containing 'h-3 w-3' icon. 2) For column header buttons: use 'h-10 w-10' (40px) which is closer to touch target minimum while keeping icon at 'h-4 w-4'. 3) Consider adding 'icon-lg' variant to button.tsx with 44x44px dimensions for critical touch targets.
ideas.user_benefit: Mobile and touch screen users can accurately tap small interactive elements without frustration or accidental misclicks, especially when removing image attachments or using Kanban column actions.

ideas.title: Add Collapsible Sidebar Navigation Sections
ideas.description: The sidebar has two fixed sections (Project and Tools) that cannot be collapsed. Allow users to collapse these sections to focus on relevant navigation items and reduce visual clutter.
ideas.rationale: Users working primarily with the Kanban board may not need to see GitHub Issues, PRs, or Worktrees sections constantly. Collapsible sections give users control over their workspace, reduce cognitive load, and are especially beneficial for users who prefer minimal interfaces. The Collapsible component already exists in the codebase.
ideas.current_state: Sidebar renders projectNavItems (7 items) and toolsNavItems (3 items) in fixed, non-collapsible sections. The collapsible.tsx component exists in ui/ folder and uses Radix UI but is not utilized in the Sidebar. Navigation is always fully expanded.
ideas.proposed_change:
Use the existing Collapsible component from ui/collapsible.tsx to wrap each navigation section. 1) Import Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger. 2) Add ChevronDown/ChevronRight icons to section headers. 3) Store collapse state in localStorage via useSettingsStore to persist preference. Pattern:
{projectNavItems.map(...)}
ideas.user_benefit: Users can customize their sidebar by collapsing sections they do not use frequently, creating a cleaner and more focused interface tailored to their current workflow.

ideas.title: Enable Electron Sandbox Mode for Defense-in-Depth
ideas.description: The Electron main window is configured with sandbox: false in apps/frontend/src/main/index.ts (line 66). While contextIsolation is enabled and nodeIntegration is disabled, the sandbox provides an additional security layer by restricting the renderer process at the OS level.
ideas.rationale: The Electron sandbox limits what code running in the renderer process can do at the operating system level. Without it, a compromised renderer (e.g., via XSS in loaded content) has more system access. This is important since the app loads external fonts from fonts.googleapis.com and may render external release notes.
ideas.currentRisk: Renderer process has fewer OS-level restrictions than recommended. If an attacker could execute code in the renderer context, they would have more capabilities than necessary.
ideas.remediation: Enable sandbox mode by setting sandbox: true in webPreferences. Review any preload script functionality that requires sandbox: false and refactor to use IPC handlers in the main process instead. Test PTY terminal integration thoroughly as node-pty may need adjustments.

ideas.title: Add Fallback Security Warning for Unencrypted Token Storage
ideas.description: In apps/frontend/src/main/claude-profile/token-encryption.ts, when Electron's safeStorage encryption is unavailable, OAuth tokens are stored in plaintext with only a console.warn. Users have no visibility that their credentials are stored insecurely.
ideas.rationale: OAuth tokens provide access to Claude AI services and potentially sensitive user data. Silent fallback to plaintext storage without user notification is a security anti-pattern. Users should be able to make informed decisions about their credential security.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
ideas.currentRisk: On systems where safeStorage is unavailable (e.g., certain Linux configurations without a keyring), OAuth tokens are stored in plaintext in settings.json, readable by any process with file access.
ideas.remediation: 1) Emit an IPC event to show a prominent UI warning when encryption fails. 2) Consider a fallback encryption using a machine-derived key (hardware ID + salt). 3) Add isTokenStoredSecurely() API for the UI to show security status. 4) Log security audit events when fallback occurs.

ideas.title: Add npm Dependency Vulnerability Scanning to CI Pipeline
ideas.description: The .github/workflows/quality-security.yml workflow runs CodeQL and Bandit for code analysis, but lacks npm audit or any JavaScript/TypeScript dependency vulnerability scanning. The frontend has 35+ runtime dependencies that could contain known CVEs.
ideas.rationale: Third-party npm packages are a common attack vector. Packages like electron, react-markdown, @xterm/xterm, and various @radix-ui components should be monitored for vulnerabilities. Supply chain attacks on npm are well-documented.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-1104: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
ideas.currentRisk: Vulnerable npm dependencies may exist without automated detection. The project uses Electron v39, xterm v6, and many UI libraries that should be continuously monitored.
ideas.remediation:
Add an npm audit job to quality-security.yml:

```yaml
npm-security:
  name: NPM Dependency Audit
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '24'
    - run: cd apps/frontend && npm ci
    - run: cd apps/frontend && npm audit --audit-level=high
```

For Python, add pip-audit to scan apps/backend/requirements.txt.

ideas.title: Replace Custom HTML Sanitization with DOMPurify
ideas.description: Two React components use dangerouslySetInnerHTML with custom regex-based HTML escaping: AppUpdateNotification.tsx (release notes) and AdvancedSettings.tsx. While the current escaping handles basic XSS (<, >, &), regex-based sanitization can miss edge cases.
ideas.rationale: Release notes come from external sources (GitHub releases API). Custom sanitizers often miss edge cases like malformed UTF-8 sequences, HTML5 entities, or SVG-based XSS. DOMPurify has been extensively tested against thousands of XSS vectors.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
ideas.currentRisk: If a crafted release note bypasses the regex sanitization, XSS could occur in the Electron renderer context. The current sanitization escapes &, <, > before processing, which is good, but a whitelist approach is safer.

ideas.title: Add Python Dependency Hash Pinning for Supply Chain Security
ideas.description: The apps/backend/requirements.txt and tests/requirements-test.txt specify dependencies with version ranges but lack cryptographic hash pinning. This leaves the project vulnerable to supply chain attacks where a malicious version could replace a legitimate one.
ideas.rationale: Supply chain attacks on Python packages (e.g., typosquatting, account compromise) are increasing. Hash pinning ensures that only verified, known-good versions are installed. Critical packages like claude-agent-sdk, graphiti-core handle AI credentials.
ideas.vulnerability: CWE-494: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
ideas.currentRisk: Dependencies are installed without cryptographic verification. A compromised PyPI package could inject malicious code into the build or development environment.
ideas.remediation:
Use pip-compile from pip-tools to generate requirements with hashes:
```bash
pip install pip-tools
pip-compile --generate-hashes requirements.in -o requirements.txt
pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt
```

Alternatively, adopt Poetry or PDM with lockfiles. Add pip-audit to CI for ongoing vulnerability scanning:
```yaml
- run: pip install pip-audit && pip-audit -r apps/backend/requirements.txt
```
